raw_response:
I will still do this year much like last year, because on 13.1 mu I cannot gamble. Wheat-maize rotation on the same land is what I know best, and with well irrigation I can push for steady yield if I feed the crop on time. I have middle school education, so I do look at fertilizer numbers and not only by feeling, but I still start from what worked in my own field and what the other good farmers around me do. For winter wheat, I will put the main fertilizer down before sowing, then give one more nitrogen topdressing at jointing with water. Wheat needs a stable stand through winter and spring, so I will not save too much on basal fertilizer. For summer maize after wheat harvest, I will use hybrid seed, keep fertilizer a bit heavier on nitrogen, and chase it once around the big bell stage with irrigation if the field shows it needs strength. Potash I will not skip, because maize on this land pulls hard, and if I only chase nitrogen the stalk grows but grain does not fill as well. Since labor in my house is only two people, I will keep management simple: rotary tillage, a few key irrigations, and only the pesticide sprays that usually matter here. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield, because one bad season hurts more than a few extra bags.
